info.name: Vestiarion: Getting Started
info.description:
From a workspace API key to a first `200`, then a first write.

1. **Set the key.** Import the Vestiarion environment, https://www.vestiarion.xyz/postman/vestiarion.postman_environment.json, choose it at the top right, and paste a workspace API key into `apiKey` as its current value. Start with a read-only key.

2. **Send steps 1 to 3.** They read the workspace's status, its invoices and the agent's decisions with its reasoning.

3. **Steps 4 and 5 add a counterparty and an invoice**, with a read-and-write key.

Each request has saved examples: its success, and each error it can answer, with the API's own message. No request can approve, reject or pay: no API call can.

Every other operation is in the "Vestiarion API reference" collection. Guide: https://www.vestiarion.xyz/docs/get-started/postman

exec: throw new Error("apiKey is empty. Choose the Vestiarion environment, top right, and paste a workspace API key into apiKey as its current value.");

variable.description: Where the API is. The Vestiarion environment sets the same value.
Set by step 4's post-response script: the counterparty step 5 adds an invoice for.
Set by step 5's pre-request script, the first time: 14 days from that day, as YYYY-MM-DD.

item.name: 1. Read, with a read-only key
item.description: Steps 1 to 3 read. A read-only key is enough, and the safest key to start with.

request.description:
The first call to make. A `200` proves the key works, and `provenance.payments` says whether payments on this workspace are live, simulated or unavailable.

What this workspace is, and what it can actually do. The first call a client should make: whether payments and yield are live, simulated or unavailable, the workspace clock, running totals, and a description of its configuration. Secrets are never included.

`unavailable` means nothing can pay in this workspace now: its Circle credentials are stored but cannot be read; or it is on Arc mainnet with no Circle account connected yet, or not live yet; or this deployment has Arc mainnet switched off. A cycle refuses to pay then rather than fall back to simulation, so status does not report it as `simulate`. Yield is also `unavailable` on a network with no yield reserve, such as Arc mainnet.

**Key:** any workspace API key; a read-only one is enough.

Reference: https://www.vestiarion.xyz/docs/api/get-status

request.description:
The ten newest invoices. Each carries the agent's verdict and why, in `agentReasoning`. Send `page.nextCursor` back as `cursor` for the next ten.

The payable and receivable book, newest first, with the row id breaking equal timestamps. Each invoice carries the agent's reasoning, not only its verdict. Only a transaction reference beginning with `0x` is exposed as `txHash`; a simulated receipt gives `null`.

An unknown `direction` or `status` is refused with `400` rather than ignored.

**Key:** any workspace API key; a read-only one is enough.

Reference: https://www.vestiarion.xyz/docs/api/list-invoices

item.name: 3. List the agent's decisions, with its reasoning

query.description: How many items to return. Defaults to 50; a larger value is capped at 200.
The previous response's `page.nextCursor`, passed back unchanged to continue. Opaque: never decode or construct one. A cursor this endpoint could not have issued is refused with `400`.
Only entries in this domain.
Only entries written by this actor.

request.description:
Every decision the agent signed into the ledger, oldest first. An entry's `detail` holds what it decided, and its reasoning where the decision records one. Tick `domain` for payables only. The saved example is the reference page's: one entry, of any actor.

The audit chain, oldest first, as a resumable stream. Because the ledger is append-only and ascending by `seq`, a stored `page.nextCursor` is a watermark: a request from it never returns an entry before it. Persist the last non-null `nextCursor` only after processing every entry in the responses read, and resume from it; the last page, which had no cursor of its own, is returned again, so de-duplicate on `seq`.

`seq` is monotonic within a workspace but not gap-free; continuity is proven by the hash chain, not by `seq`.

**Key:** any workspace API key; a read-only one is enough.

Reference: https://www.vestiarion.xyz/docs/api/list-ledger-entries

item.name: 2. Add records, with a read-and-write key
item.description:
Steps 4 and 5 add records, and need a key created with **Can also add records** ticked: switch `apiKey` to one. A read-only key gets `403 forbidden`, as the saved examples show.

Adding is all a key does. The agent decides the invoice as one typed into the console, under every guardrail, and pays nothing to the counterparty's address until a person in the workspace confirms it. The `Idempotency-Key` header makes each step safe to send twice: a repeat within 24 hours gets the first answer back and adds nothing.

header.description: Makes a retry safe: up to 255 printable ASCII characters, unique to the record being added, such as its id in your own system. A repeat with the same key and the same body within 24 hours gets the first answer back, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and adds nothing. The same key with a different body answers `409`.

request.description:
Adds a vendor, screened as one added in the console. Its post-response script keeps its `id` as `{{counterpartyId}}` for step 5.

Adds a vendor, contractor or client, checked by the rules of the console's form and screened as one added there: the answer's `riskLevel` is the screening's verdict, or `unscreened` when screening could not finish. It is recorded in the ledger as `create_counterparty` with `via: "api"` and the key's id.

An address added through the API waits for a person. The agent pays nothing to it until an owner, admin or approver confirms it on Counterparties, so a key can add records but cannot point the agent's payments at a new address.

**Key:** a read-and-write key. A read-only key gets `403 forbidden`.

Reference: https://www.vestiarion.xyz/docs/api/create-counterparty

response.name: 201 Created

request.description:
Adds a payable from the counterparty step 4 added, due in 14 days. Follow the agent's decision on it with step 2, or in the console.

Adds a payable or a receivable, checked by the rules of the console's invoice form, and recorded in the ledger as `create_invoice` with `via: "api"` and the key's id. It is added as the key's issuer's: if the agent holds it, the issuer cannot approve it, unless they are the workspace's only approver.

The agent decides a payable as one typed in, with every guardrail and the workspace's limits, usually within a minute. The API never approves or pays. A `counterpartyId` the workspace does not hold, including another workspace's, answers `400`.

**Key:** a read-and-write key. A read-only key gets `403 forbidden`.

Reference: https://www.vestiarion.xyz/docs/api/create-invoice
